title: Evaluating RAG Systems with Automated Metrics
description: Measure RAG system quality using faithfulness, answer relevance, context precision, and context recall metrics with .NET evaluation frameworks.

data.text: Why RAG Evaluation Differs from Traditional QA

Traditional question-answering has a single correct answer. RAG systems have two quality dimensions: (1) Does the generated answer faithfully reflect the provided context (no hallucinations)? and (2) Does the system retrieve the right context to answer the question correctly? Evaluating RAG requires metrics for both dimensions, which is why simple accuracy falls short.

rows: Does the answer match the provided context?
LLM judge: compare answer to context quotes
Is the answer relevant to the question?
LLM judge: label each passage relevant/irrelevant
Did we retrieve enough context to answer?
LLM judge: could the answer be derived from context?
Does the answer match ground truth?

data.text: Manual evaluation is slow and subjective. Automated RAG evaluation uses LLM judges (typically GPT-4 or Claude) to score system outputs against ground truth or reference answers. The evaluation pipeline takes a question, generates a context plus answer, then runs the judge LLM with a structured rubric.

data.text: RAG systems fail in predictable ways. Understanding these failure modes is key to targeted improvement: (1) No context retrieved (retrieval failure), (2) Wrong context retrieved (irrelevant passages), (3) Context too long (LLM ignores it), (4) Context too short (LLM hallucinates), (5) Format mismatch (context in wrong format for the LLM).

data.title: Failure Mode Classification
data.content: Classifying RAG failures to guide remediation:

data.text: Do not rely on a single metric. A system can score high on faithfulness but low on answer correctness — the LLM is confidently wrong but grounded in wrong context. Always evaluate the full matrix: faithfulness plus answer relevance plus context precision plus context recall plus factuality.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: RAG has two quality dimensions: answer groundedness and context quality
Five core metrics: faithfulness, answer relevance, context precision, context recall, factuality
Use LLM judges with structured rubrics for automated evaluation
Classify failure modes to guide targeted fixes
Run evaluation on a diverse benchmark dataset of 100+ queries per iteration
data.takeaway: RAG evaluation is multi-dimensional. Automated LLM-judge pipelines combined with failure mode classification enable data-driven iteration on retrieval and generation quality.
